title: Bring your archive home.
subtitle: Download folders from Google Drive. Keep original files, dates and embedded location data.
not_connected: Connect your project to get started.
download_hint: Open a folder on the left, then choose a destination on your device.
folder_placeholder: Choose a folder or enter its full path
choose_folder: Choose a folder on this device
parallel_hint: Start with 4. Fewer connections can help on an unstable network.
preserve_hint: Original bytes. No resizing, previews or changes to embedded metadata.
documents_notice: Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and shortcuts are listed in the report but are not exported in this version.
connect_to_browse: Connect Google Drive to see your files.
resume_hint: You can close the interface. Downloads continue while the app is running.
quota_explanation: These counters cover only this app on this device. They are estimates, not Google's remaining quota or a billing balance. Other apps and devices are not included.
limited_hint: Number of limit responses received from Google
limits_hint: Enter your project's values from Google Cloud Console. Saving these numbers changes the display only, not your actual Google quotas.
cost_notice: Defaults are documentation references dated 29 October 2026, not verified limits for your project. The 1 TB value is a published pricing threshold, not a guaranteed hard cutoff or a price quote. API conditions can change. Meter values do not stop downloads.
footer: Files stay on your device. Independent open-source application.
testing_notice: Google limits Testing authorizations to seven days. Personal-use exceptions and publication requirements must be checked for your project. In production status, an unverified-app warning may still appear.
privacy: The app reads your Drive and saves chosen originals locally. OAuth credentials are stored in the operating system's credential store when available; otherwise they stay in memory for this session. They are never written to a plaintext token file.
configured: Project ready. Sign in to continue.
signin_pending: Complete sign-in in the browser. Waiting up to three minutes…
credentials_saved: Connection saved in the system credential store.
credentials_memory: Connection is kept for this session only. You may need to reconnect after restarting.
loading: Asking Google Drive for this folder…
empty_folder: There are no files on this page.
file_imported: Project imported. Click Connect Google Drive.
shutdown_notice: The app is stopping. Current file parts are being saved. You can close this tab.
connect_google: Google Drive is not connected. Click Connect Google Drive.
desktop_json_required: The app needs the JSON for a Desktop app OAuth client. Create that client in Google Cloud Console and choose its JSON file.
auth_pending: Google sign-in is already open. Complete it in the browser first.
credential_store_unavailable: The operating system's credential store is unavailable. Check its permissions or unlock it, then try again.
drive_permission_required: Google did not grant read access to Drive. Sign in again and allow the requested access.
google_signin_failed: Google sign-in did not finish. Check your client JSON, test-user list and browser message, then try again.
google_signin_expired: Google access expired or was revoked. Reconnect Google Drive; saved files remain on your device.
internet_unavailable: The app could not reach Google over the internet, or the connection broke. Check your network and continue the task.
transfer_incomplete: The transfer ended before the complete file arrived. The app will retry from its saved part. If paused, check your connection and continue the task.
google_quota: Google Drive limited requests or downloads. Wait before continuing. Your file parts are preserved.
google_download_denied: Google Drive denied this download. Check the file's sharing settings, the account used and the owner's download restrictions.
google_file_missing: Google Drive could not find this file, or your account no longer has access.
google_unavailable: Google Drive returned an unexpected response. Try again later. File parts are preserved.
google_invalid_response: Google Drive returned incomplete or invalid file information. Refresh the folder and try again.
google_incomplete_list: Google Drive did not provide a complete file list. The task is paused so files are not silently skipped. Continue to retry.
google_document_unsupported: This is a Google document or shortcut. This version downloads original stored files only; it does not export documents or follow shortcuts.
unsafe_path: Local files: this path contains an unsafe name, symbolic link or junction. Choose an ordinary destination folder.
name_collision: Local files: a destination name is already occupied. No existing file was overwritten. Choose another folder or retry.
partial_changed: Local files: a saved file part was changed and cannot be trusted. Keep it for inspection and start a new task for this file in the same destination.
source_changed: Google Drive changed the file during download. The app will retry with its new version.
integrity_failed: The downloaded file did not match its expected size or checksum. It was not published as a completed file. Start a new task to retry it.
range_invalid: Google Drive returned an invalid file range. The app kept the saved part and did not combine incompatible data.
low_space: Local drive: less than 500 MB of safe free space remains. Free space, then continue the task. Saved files and parts are kept.
local_unavailable: Local drive: the app could not read or write the destination. Check that the drive or network folder is connected and writable, then continue.
application_failed: The local application could not complete this operation. Restart it and continue the saved task. If it happens again, report a problem.
timestamp_failed: The file was saved, but the local filesystem did not accept its modification date. Embedded photo metadata is unchanged.
task_active: Another task is still running or saving its progress. Pause it and wait for the paused status before starting another.
task_missing: This task no longer exists in the local history. Refresh the page.
different_account: This task belongs to a different Google account or project. Connect the original account and project before continuing.
invalid_file_id: The Google Drive file identifier is invalid. Refresh the folder.
invalid_request: The local app could not understand the request. Refresh the page and try again.
local_request_required: This operation must be requested from DiskDownloader's own local interface. Open the app's browser window.
folder_picker_failed: The app could not open the system folder picker. Enter the destination's full path manually.
request_timeout: The local app did not respond in time. Check its status window before repeating the command.
service_unreachable: The browser cannot reach the local app. Start DiskDownloader and reopen its interface.
limits_saved: Reference values saved. Actual Google quotas were not changed.
guide_description: One small step at a time, from your Google account to your first download.
guide_saved: Your place is saved on this device.
guide_import_waiting: Choose the JSON you downloaded in the previous step.

guide_steps.title: Start with the account that holds your files
guide_steps.intro: You will create your own Google project, then let this app read your Drive.

actions.title: Open Google Drive.
actions.body: Sign in at drive.google.com. Use the account whose files you want to save; check the account picture in the top-right corner.

actions.title: Find a small folder to try first.
actions.body: Make sure its files are visible. Leave that tab open and keep DiskDownloader running while you follow this guide.

actions.title: Keep this guide nearby.
actions.body: Google pages open in another tab. Return here after each step; Back and Next only move through the instructions.

guide_steps.check: You know which Google account and folder you will use.
guide_steps.note: A Google Cloud project identifies your own copy of the app. This app reads Drive content and saves it on your device; it does not upload your archive to the developer.

guide_steps.title: Create your personal Google Cloud project
guide_steps.intro: Use the same project throughout the Google Cloud steps.

actions.title: Open the project creation page.
actions.body: Sign in if asked. If this is your first visit, read and accept Google’s terms if you agree.

actions.title: Name the project.
actions.body: Enter DiskDownloader Personal as the project name. Keep the automatically generated project ID. Use No organization if it is available for your personal account.

actions.title: Create it and select it.
actions.body: Click Create and wait. Use the project selector at the top of the console to select DiskDownloader Personal.

guide_steps.check: Your project name appears in the console’s top project selector.
guide_steps.note: If project creation is blocked on a work or school account, ask its administrator about access. If you already have a suitable project, select it and continue.

guide_steps.title: Turn on the Google Drive API
guide_steps.intro: The API is the connection this app uses to list and download your Drive files.

actions.title: Check the selected project.
actions.body: Confirm the top project selector still shows your DiskDownloader project.

actions.title: Open the Drive API page.
actions.body: Use the button below, or open APIs & Services → Library and search for Google Drive API. Choose that exact API.

actions.title: Enable it.
actions.body: Click Enable and wait for the API overview. If the page already offers Manage or Disable, the API is enabled.

guide_steps.check: Google Drive API is enabled for your selected project.
guide_steps.note: Google Photos and Google Cloud Storage are different services. This app needs Google Drive API.

guide_steps.title: Give the connection a name
guide_steps.intro: These details identify your own app on Google’s sign-in screen.

actions.title: Open Branding.
actions.body: In the console menu, open Google Auth platform → Branding, or use the button below.

actions.title: Start configuration.
actions.body: If Google says the platform is not configured, click Get Started. Enter DiskDownloader Personal for the app name.

actions.title: Choose your email.
actions.body: For User support email, choose your own email address. Click Next to reach the audience screen.

guide_steps.check: The app has a name and your support email; the next screen asks about its audience.
guide_steps.note: If configuration already exists, check its app name and support email in Branding, save any changes, and continue. Google may translate its menu labels.

guide_steps.title: Set up the app for your personal account
guide_steps.intro: A personal Gmail account uses the External audience.

actions.title: Choose External.
actions.body: On the audience screen, select External and continue. Internal is for accounts restricted to a Google Workspace organization.

actions.title: Enter a contact email.
actions.body: Use your own address on the contact information screen so Google can contact you about this project.

actions.title: Finish configuration.
actions.body: Review the requested Google policies. If you agree, accept them, continue, and create the configuration.

guide_steps.check: Google Auth platform is configured for your project.
guide_steps.note: If you configured this project before, open Audience to check its audience. Work or school policies may restrict which audience types you can use.

guide_steps.title: Allow your account to use the test app
guide_steps.intro: While the project is in Testing, the account you sign in with must be on its test-user list.

actions.title: Open Audience.
actions.body: Keep the personal setup in Testing. Find the Test users section.

actions.title: Add your Drive account.
actions.body: Click Add users. Enter the full email address of the account holding your files, then save it.

actions.title: Check the saved address.
actions.body: Confirm the account appears in the list. You will choose this same account when signing in from DiskDownloader.

guide_steps.check: Your Google Drive account is listed under Test users.
guide_steps.note: Drive authorizations in Testing normally expire after seven days, so you may need to reconnect. Switching to In production does not itself verify the app. For an existing production project, follow Google’s rules for its publishing status.

guide_steps.title: Add permission to read your Drive
guide_steps.intro: Use the exact read-only scope below so the app can retrieve your stored originals.

actions.title: Open Data Access.
actions.body: Choose Data Access in Google Auth platform, then Add or Remove Scopes.

actions.title: Find the read-only Drive scope.
actions.body: Search for drive.readonly. If the scope is not listed, use Google’s manual entry field for the exact address below.

actions.title: Update and save.
actions.body: Select that scope, apply the selection, and save the Data Access page. Do not substitute the metadata-only scope: it cannot download the original content.

guide_steps.check: The Data Access page includes the full drive.readonly scope below.
guide_steps.note: This permission lets the app read Drive files without editing or deleting them. Google classifies some scopes as restricted; personal-use and verification requirements depend on how the project is used.

guide_steps.title: Create an OAuth client for this app
guide_steps.intro: The client tells Google that you are connecting a desktop application.

actions.title: Open Clients.
actions.body: Choose Clients in Google Auth platform, then Create Client.

actions.title: Choose Desktop app.
actions.body: Set Application type to Desktop app and name it DiskDownloader Desktop. This is a normal desktop app, not an AI agent.

actions.title: Create the client.
actions.body: Click Create. Keep the resulting client dialog open for the next step.

guide_steps.check: A Desktop app OAuth client has been created.
guide_steps.note: If the form asks for authorized JavaScript origins or web redirect URLs, check the application type. An API key or service-account key cannot replace the Desktop app client JSON.

guide_steps.title: Save the client JSON to your computer
guide_steps.intro: DiskDownloader imports this file so you do not have to paste client details.

actions.title: Download the JSON now.
actions.body: Use Download JSON in the client creation dialog. Your browser usually saves it in Downloads.

actions.title: Keep the downloaded file as it is.
actions.body: It normally has a long name ending in .json. You do not need to rename it, open it in an editor, or copy its contents.

actions.title: Return to DiskDownloader.
actions.body: Keep the file on this device. The next step opens a file picker to select it.

guide_steps.check: You can find the downloaded client .json file in your Downloads folder.
guide_steps.note: Google may only show a client secret when the client is created. If you cannot obtain a complete client JSON later, create a new Desktop app client and download its JSON immediately.

guide_steps.title: Choose the file in DiskDownloader
guide_steps.intro: Use the button below; you can complete this step without closing the guide.

actions.title: Open the file picker.
actions.body: Click Choose client JSON below and go to your Downloads folder.

actions.title: Select the downloaded JSON.
actions.body: Choose the file from the previous step and open it. The app checks that it is a Desktop app client configuration.

actions.title: Check the project status.
actions.body: The status below will confirm the import and show your Google Cloud project ID.

guide_steps.check: The status confirms that the client JSON has been imported.
guide_steps.note: If the file is rejected, return to Clients and check that it was created as Desktop app. Keep the JSON private rather than attaching it to an issue or message.

guide_steps.title: Authorize the connection in your browser
guide_steps.intro: The sign-in opens in your system browser. Keep the app running.

actions.title: Start the connection.
actions.body: Click Connect Google Drive below. The button becomes available after importing the client JSON.

actions.title: Choose your test account.
actions.body: Select the account you added in Audience → Test users. Review the app name and the requested Drive read permission before allowing access.

actions.title: Return here when Google is finished.
actions.body: The status below changes to Connected when the app receives the result. If sign-in times out, start the connection again.

guide_steps.check: The live connection status says Connected.
guide_steps.note: An access-blocked error often means the chosen account is missing from Test users, or an organization policy blocks the app. An unverified-app notice can appear for your own test project: check that its name and permissions match what you created before using Google’s Advanced/continue option, if Google offers it.

guide_steps.title: Save a small folder first
guide_steps.intro: Your connection is ready. Finish the guide to reach the file browser.

actions.title: Open a Drive folder.
actions.body: In the source panel, click the folder name you want. Download this folder saves its contents, including subfolders.

actions.title: Choose a destination on your device.
actions.body: Use the folder-picker button or enter a full path. Start with four simultaneous files, then click Download this folder.

actions.title: Check the result.
actions.body: Follow the task until it finishes, then open its CSV report. For an interrupted task, use Continue / check missing files with the same account and destination.

guide_steps.check: Your files are saved and you have checked the task report.
guide_steps.note: Closing the browser tab leaves the app running. Use Exit application to stop it. Keep your cloud copy while checking your first download. Google-native documents and shortcuts are listed as unsupported.
